content:
London. Four years ago, a European spacecraft has started observing from close range the asteroid that the American space agency NASA had hit during Earth's defense test.

As announced by the European Space Agency (ESA) on Wednesday, the spacecraft named 'Hera' is currently studying the asteroid 'Didymos' and its small moon 'Dimorphos' from a distance of 25 to 30 kilometers.

To test whether Earth can be protected from potentially fatal space rocks in the future, NASA had deliberately crashed its 'DART' spacecraft into Dimorphos in 2022. That collision had shortened the orbit of Dimorphos around Didymos and also caused a slight change in its path around the sun.

The Hera spacecraft, the size of a small car launched in 2024, will reach even closer to the asteroid next month, at a distance of 20 kilometers. ESA officials consider this mission as a 'crash site investigation' to be conducted by their best robotic spy.

Hera spacecraft carries 25 scientific instruments along with two shoebox-sized 'CubeSats'. These instruments will conduct a more detailed survey of Dimorphos and will also attempt to land on it.

When the DART (Double Asteroid Redirection Test) spacecraft collided, rocks and fragments of debris were ejected from Dimorphos, which further propelled the impact's momentum.

The trail of ejected debris spread for thousands of kilometers in space for months. Scientists estimate that some of those debris might still be in the vicinity. Dimorphos, with a diameter of approximately 151 meters (500 feet), is smaller compared to Didymos, which has a diameter of about 780 meters.
